text: Are the stereotypes about women true? I continue with my take on stereotypes she is talking about. Number two, women are dramatic and overreact. Studies found that men who express anger in professional settings received a boost in perceived status. Women who expressed the exact same emotion consistently given lower status, lower wages, and were seen as less competent. Translation, men get rewarded for anger, women get punished for it. Same reactions to completely different outcomes based entirely on gender. Knowledge is extremely powerful. She most likely refers to the Breskow and Ullman 2008 anger study. Where participants evaluated male versus female professionals who expressed the same controlled anger in a professional setting. The findings were that men on average were seen as more competent, higher status, and sometimes even more hireable. So that part is true. I guess her point is that the same behavior can be judged differently simply based on gender. And if that is the case, then labels like too emotional or overreacting may indeed be influenced by bias and not always reflect reality. There is a slight inconsistency though. The study she mentioned specifically tested controlled professional anger. So jumping from the same assertive anger is judged differently to women are unfairly called dramatic in general, is a bit of a stretch because the study didn't test for overreacting or dramatic behavior. But this topic is actually closely related to the stereotype that women are more emotional, which we addressed in part two. And again, it depends a lot on how you define emotional. If by emotional we mean being more expressive and open about feelings, then women on average do show higher levels of emotional expressiveness and score higher in neuroticism. On the other hand, men are also emotional, just differently. Instead of talking about emotions, they are more likely to act on them, especially when it comes to anger, frustration, and aggression. So if being dramatic means being more emotionally expressive, then women may appear more dramatic. But if overreacting means acting physically on emotions, then men may actually do it more. So in the end, both men and women can be dramatic and overreact. And without a clear definition of what those terms actually mean, it is very hard to say who does it more.
